        refuse(call_id, name, "not_found", "the turn range holds no block")
    chars = {str(r.get("hash") or ""): int(r.get("chars") or 0) for r in rows(lg, "r-chars")}
    raw = sum(chars.get(str(r.get("hash") or ""), 0) for r in span)
    if READ_BUDGET is not None and raw > RAW_FACTOR * READ_BUDGET:
        refuse(call_id, name, "too_large",
               "the turn range is many times larger than the read budget; ask for fewer turns",
               budget_said({"raw_size": raw, "block_count": len(span)}))
    hashes = sorted({str(r.get("hash") or "") for r in span})
    turn = str(ctx.get("turn_id") or "")
    emit([lstore([("r-range", range_rows(args)),
                  ("r-blocks", sel("blocks", ["hash", "body"], {"hash": {"in": hashes}}))]
                 + marks_reads(turn, hashes), "read-range-3", call_id, carry(name, args))])

if phase == "read-range-3":
    span = shown(span_of(args, rows(lg, "r-range")))
    bodies = bodies_of(lg, "r-blocks")
    own = own_history(span, bodies)
    kept = [r for r in span if int(r.get("seq") or 0) not in own]
    size = size_of(bodies.get(str(r.get("hash") or ""), "") for r in kept)
    if over_budget(size):
        refuse(call_id, name, "too_large",
               "the turn range is larger than the read budget; ask for fewer turns,"
               " or read a block by its id, in pages",
               budget_said({"size": size, "block_count": len(kept)}))
    window = release_window(lg)
    if window is None:
        refuse(call_id, name, "too_large", CUT[name], budget_said({}))
    released = released_hashes(window, sorted({str(r.get("hash") or "") for r in kept}))
    entries = []
    for r in kept:
        e = entry_of(r, element_of(bodies.get(str(r.get("hash") or ""))))
        e["released"] = str(r.get("hash") or "") in released
        entries.append(e)
    out = [answer(call_id, name, {"blocks": entries, "size": size,
                                  "skipped_history": len(span) - len(kept),
                                  "from_turn": args.get("from_turn"),
                                  "to_turn": args.get("to_turn")})]
    ops = reread_ops(released, rows(lg, "r-mine"))
    if ops:
        out.append(lstore(ops, "reread", call_id, ""))
    emit(out)

if phase == "outline":
    wall, marks = rows(lg, "o-wall"), rows(lg, "o-marks")
    bound = ROWS_MAX if args.get("rows_max") else SCAN_BUDGET
    # The outline reaches the newest `scan_budget` rows this round may see
    # (GH #925, OR-BD-74): hidden rows that fill the first read send it once
    # more, to the row bound.
    if not args.get("rows_max") and (
            (len(wall) > SCAN_BUDGET and len(shown(wall)) < len(wall))
            or (len(marks) >= SCAN_BUDGET and len(shown(marks)) < len(marks))):
        emit([outline_reads(dict(args, rows_max=True))])
    seen, noted = shown(wall), shown(marks)
    # Where the row bound leaves open which are the newest `scan_budget` rows
    # -- or `topic` marks -- the round may see, the outline answers in the cut
    # form: the sessions out of what it read counted the hidden rows (closing
    # review I-2). The topics come out of the newest `scan_budget` marks it
    # may see, as without hidden ones: one hidden mark among 15 used to bring
    # all 15 in and a topic the budget's ten do not open (OR-BD-86 driver).
    if args.get("rows_max") and ((len(seen) <= SCAN_BUDGET and len(wall) > bound)
                                 or (len(noted) < SCAN_BUDGET and len(marks) >= bound)):
        out = {"sessions": [], "truncated_scan": True, "detail": CUT[name]}
        if args.get("since"):
            out["since"] = args["since"]
        emit([answer(call_id, name, out)])
    # Sessions, turns and topics out of the rows and `topic` marks this round
    # may see (GH #925): a hidden mark neither opens nor closes a topic. The
    # newest `scan_budget` rows, those of them whose turn lies at or after
    # `since` (OR-KF-21); cut short only where the next row read is one too.
    span = seen[:SCAN_BUDGET]
    wall = list(reversed([r for r in span if inside(args, r)]))
    truncated = len(seen) > SCAN_BUDGET and inside(args, seen[SCAN_BUDGET])
    window = noted[:SCAN_BUDGET]
    marks = list(reversed(window))
    if len(window) >= SCAN_BUDGET:
        # The marks read are full: the mark that named the open topic may
        # lie before them (A7). The newest one that says something, when it
        # does lie there and does not end its topic, opens the list.
        low = min(int(m.get("seq") or 0) for m in window)
        seed = next(iter(shown(rows(lg, "o-seed"))), None)
        t = topic_of((seed or {}).get("value"))
        if seed is not None and int(seed.get("seq") or 0) < low and t and t[0] != "end":
            marks = [seed] + marks
    emit([answer(call_id, name, outline_answer(wall, marks, args.get("since"), truncated))])

park("store answer in unknown phase %r -- dropped" % phase)

scan_budget.description: The most wall rows the round may see that one `history_search` reads, newest first (and one outline); a search that stops there says `truncated_scan` with `cut_by` `scan_budget` and answers with the hits up to that point, a turn range with more such rows is refused with `too_large`; `released` of a `history_read` is decided by the newest this many `release`/`pin` marks of its blocks the round may see. Rows of other rounds count toward no budget, but every read stops at twice this many rows in all (GH #925, GH #931). Where that row bound leaves the answer open, the call answers in the cut form and shows nothing it read: a search `hits` [], `cut_by` `scan_budget`, a `detail` and no `scanned` or `total_hits`; a `history_read` `too_large` with a `detail` and no `block_count_at_least`; an outline no sessions. The form is the same on every wall that reaches the bound, so there rows of other rounds move one bit per call and never a count; it takes at least this many of them among the first twice this + 1 rows one read meets (of a read's `release`/`pin` marks, more than this many among their newest twice this), or for the neighbours of a search with `context` at least this / hits - `context` - 3 of the hit's session on one side. Below the bound every number an answer carries counts rows the round may see, but where a page ends and how long a read takes still depend on rows of other rounds (GH #932). The round loses that call's answer; a narrower `since`/`until` brings it back (OR-BD-86).

time_budget_ms.description: The most time one `history_search` spends, from the call on; a match that runs past it is interrupted and the search answers with the hits up to that point (`truncated_scan`, `cut_by` `time_budget`). Below `external_timeout_ms`, so the answer always comes before the runner would kill the child.

page_rows.description: The wall rows the round may see that one page of a search matches per ledger round trip; a search stops at the page that fills its `limit` (`stopped_at_limit`).

place.description: GH #1279: the place of the person (a town, a locale) a view names in its leaf `frame` and the seed's fact line as `place:`; the composition renders it from the profile. "" (the default) names no place.

timezone.description: GH #1279: the IANA zone (`Europe/Berlin`) the moment of a view (`frame`) and of the seed's fact line is given in (`iso` with its offset, `weekday`, `timezone`). "" (the default) or an unknown zone is UTC, the latter said on stderr.

now_utc.description: GH #1279: a fixed instant (RFC 3339, UTC) for the moment of a view and a seed, the test override of its wall-clock read. "" (the default) reads the clock; since GH #1479 also the instant a seed holds the `until` of a `once` note against (OR-d58-2.followup.4).

seed_entries_max.description: The most session and until notes one `seed` carries in its `Notes:` line -- the best ranked, `priority` first (0 first), then the youngest, shown oldest first; the rest stays out of the seed and is said on stderr (the live feed's facts still count every note). 0 (the default) carries every note.

seed_budget.description: The tokens one `seed` (the start window of a running session) holds, by the token-estimate block: the newest turns that fit, the oldest left out first; the fact line, the notes, the held lines and the anchor always stand. 8192 (the default) is the window as it was. The ask for a start window names no target, so no catalog row sizes it; a set sets it.

seed_anchor.description: The persona's anchor, one `developer` line a `seed` ends on -- after the turns and a held `hint`, right before a held `wind_down` (the end of the call stays last), in the head before the turns only with `seed_anchor_first` "1" (GH #1402); counted in the seed's budget. "" (the default) adds nothing.

seed_anchor_first.description: #1402: "1" puts `seed_anchor` at the end of the seed's head (after the facts, a held `identity` line and the notes), in front of the turns, instead of into the tail; "0" (the default) keeps it in the tail. Without an anchor nothing moves.

seed_renew_line.description: #1402: the set's wait line of a renewed session -- on an `in_seed_ask` whose `hop.reason` is `renew` or `recover` the LAST `developer` line of the seed, after the anchor and a held `wind_down`; never on `start`; counted in the seed's budget. "" (the default) adds nothing.

seed_target.description: D58 judge (GH #1480): the target whose family a start window (`seed`) and the live facts and live feed of a running session carry -- the contributions the domains leave for it (`in_part`, a curate's `parts`), one fact per source, never read. A seed reads those without a subject; its fact line names what each source's contribution names (`<source>: <name>, ...`, in the order of the sources). The same name in `./history` and `./policy`. "" (the default) = none.

topic_aging.description: GH #1436: "1" lets the topic age -- one rule in `./history` (the topic handed to the route stamp, the judge and a seed) and `./policy` (the topic of a call's live feed): it frames no turn of a call opened after it was named, none of a session it was not last named in, and none once `topic_age_turns` turns passed without a renewed mention. "0" (the default) = the reads and answers as before, byte for byte.

topic_age_turns.description: GH #1436: with `topic_aging` "1" the turns without a renewed mention after which a topic frames no turn any more; counted by the person's rows on the wall (one per turn), not by marks.

topic_age_rows.description: GH #1436: with `topic_aging` "1" the bound of the read that counts the turns since the topic was named (the person's rows, newest first); a read that comes back full without reaching the naming counts as `topic_age_turns` turns. Keep it above `topic_age_turns`.

notes_latest_per_item.description: D38 V1 (GH #1451, review o15-Rv1 m2): the window's knob of `./policy` in the seed -- "1" reads `notes.item` and the seed (and `live_facts`) carries only the youngest note of one `(source, item)`; a note without an item stays. "0" (the default) the seed of before.

part_rows.description: D58 judge (GH #1480): the most contributions one read of a target's family takes, per range (the contributions without a subject, and those about the round's person); a read that comes back full is said on stderr. The same number in `./history` and `./policy`.

seed_line_rows.description: D58 judge (GH #1480): the most held start window lines one seed reads of each lifetime (`always`, and `session` of the running session); a read that comes back full is said on stderr and the rest waits.

seed_anchor_order.description: D58 judge (GH #1480): the persona anchor's place among the tail lines of a seed -- a tail line (`in_seed_line` `position` `tail`) of a lower `order` stands before it, one of the same or a higher order after it. 1.5 (the default) keeps today's senders' start window byte for byte (a hint at order 1 before the anchor, the wind-down at order 2 after it). Without effect when `seed_anchor_first` is "1".

note_once.description: D58 note (GH #1477): "1" = an open note of scope `once` stands in the next start window (`seed`) of its round, among the notes of the `Notes:` line and under `seed_entries_max`; the seed that carries it uses it up for its call (`notes.used_turn` = the call, written only while empty) and a note with a `receipt` answers on `note_receipt`; the renewals of the same call carry it on and answer nothing, every other window never sees it again. A `once` note whose `until` lies behind the seed's clock (`now_utc`, else the wall clock) is not shown and answers nothing (GH #1479). Reads `notes.receipt`. The same knob in `./intake` and `./policy`. "0" (the default) the seed of before, byte for byte.

session_id.description: on `seed`: the `session_id` of the `seed_ask`, given back unchanged with `live` and `renewal_n`; on `live_facts`: the `session_id` of the `in_live_end`, given back with `live` (#1369); on `note_receipt` (D58 note, GH #1477): the session the note was shown in -- the `seed_ask`'s `session_id`, else its `live`

note_source.description: on `note_receipt` (D58 note, GH #1477): the `source` of the shown note

note_id.description: on `note_receipt` (D58 note, GH #1477): the `id` of the shown note

receipt.description: on `note_receipt` (D58 note, GH #1477): the note's `receipt` as its sender gave it, never read by the curator

turn_id.description: on `note_receipt` (D58 note, GH #1477): the turn the note was shown in -- "" from a start window, which belongs to no turn

target.description: on `note_receipt` (D58 note, GH #1477): the target of the call that showed the note -- "" from a start window, whose question names none

at.description: on `note_receipt` (D58 note, GH #1477): when the note was used up, RFC 3339 UTC

description.purpose: The model reads its own wall (GH #893): `history_search` (phrase, exact text or regular expression, newest first, with time, kind, limit and neighbour bounds, page by page and within a time budget), `history_read` (one block by its id `#<12 hex>`, or a turn range, whole or refused with `too_large`) and `history_outline` (sessions with their turn ranges and the topics their `topic` marks opened and closed, OR-KY-71), answered out of this hive's ledger alone. The model's own `history_*` calls and their answers are no hits and no blocks of a range. A read of a block TRIM released writes one `reread` mark per block and turn. Every row of `wall` and `marks` it reads passes the audience gate of the round the call is served in (`context.audience_set`, GH #925): a row whose audience does not hold the round, or that has none, is no hit, no neighbour, no block of a range, no id and no session, turn or topic of the outline -- an id or a turn the round may not see is `not_found` in the words an unknown one gets. A `reread` mark carries the round's audience. Since D58 GH #1480 it answers the internal lane `in_view_ask` of any composition: a VIEW, the curator's short way to a window for a named target, only read and handed back to the asker -- `messages` (the last `turns` turns of the running generation and round, never the running turn, oldest first, within `budget_tokens`, at most 4000, 1500 at or below 0 or without one; with a target both sides, without one the person's words alone, as GH #1304 gave them) and, with a target, `system` (`frame`, the aged topic, the target's family of contributions). `in_seed_ask` answers one `seed` (the round's newest turns of both roles within `seed_budget` tokens, shipped 8192, behind one fact line, the held seed line last; an ask without the handle `live` gets an empty one), and `in_part` (a contribution to a target's section) / `in_seed_line` (a start window line) keep one `state` row each.
description.use_when: Inside the curator only; the parent routes `hop.tool_name` with the prefix `history_` to the hive's `in_history_call` lane and takes `tool_result` back into its collector's `in_tool`.
description.not_in_scope: No model, no embedding, no ranking: deterministic ledger reads. No other model's wall -- the ledger is this hive's. The schemas the model is offered are the curator's menu answer (`HISTORY_SCHEMAS` in `./schemas`, spliced into `CURATOR_OFFER`), not this cell's.
description.emits_meaning: tool_result: the answer to one call, one `tool_result` turn under its call id, the text a JSON object; a refusal names its code in the text and in `hop.error_code` (bad_arguments, bad_pattern, bad_range, not_found, ambiguous, too_large, unknown_tool, ledger_error, missing_audience -- a round that declares no audience, refused before anything is read; empty on an answer). A search cut short is an answer (`truncated_scan`, `cut_by` `scan_budget` or `time_budget`; `stopped_at_limit`). lstore: ledger reads, and the `reread` marks. view (D58 GH #1480): the answer to one `in_view_ask`, exactly one, `{messages: [{origin, type: "text", text}], system?, truncated}` -- the earlier turns oldest first without the running one (with a target both sides, without one the person's words alone) within `budget_tokens`; with a target `system`, a tree of leaves `{text}`: `frame` (the moment: `now`, `weekday`, `timezone`, `place`, one fact per line), `topic` (when there is one, aged) and the target's family `{<source>: leaf}` (when it holds a contribution); `hop.refused` `no_round` (no round, nothing read) or `bad_arguments` (`turns` below 1 without a target), `hop.degraded` `store` (a refused ledger read), both absent on an answer. seed: the answer to one `in_seed_ask`, exactly one, `{messages: [{role, text}], est_tokens, context}` -- `messages` one `developer` fact line, a `developer` line `Notes: ...` of the session and until notes (with `note_once` "1" also the open `once` notes, D58 note, GH #1477), the turns as `user`/`assistant` and the inner turns as `developer` lines `(<kind>) <text>`, the held `in_seed_line` last as `developer`; `est_tokens` by the estimate the budget counts with; the facts it carried are written as `seed_facts:<live>` for the live feed; `hop.live`, `hop.renewal_n` given back; `hop.refused` `no_live` (no handle: nothing read, nothing written), `no_round` or `hop.degraded` `store` with `messages: []`. live_facts (#1369): the answer to one `in_live_end`, exactly one, `{messages: [], live, session_id, seed_used, facts: [{source, id, text}], delegations: [{turn_id, text}]}` -- read only, the session's `seed_facts:<live>` stays; `hop.live`, `hop.session_id` given back; `hop.refused` `no_round`/`no_live` or `hop.degraded` `store` with `seed_used` false and empty lists. note_receipt (D58 note, GH #1477, only with `note_once` "1"): one per open `once` note with a `receipt` that a `seed` of a running session carries for the first time, sent with that `seed` -- `{messages: []}`, every field in the head: `note_source`, `note_id`, `receipt`, `session_id`, `turn_id` "", `target` "", `at`; a renewal of the same session carries the note on and sends none.
description.consumes_meaning: in_history_call (one `tool_call` turn, `hop.tool_call_id`, `hop.tool_name`, the round in `context.audience_set`) and the ledger's answers to its phases (search-rows, search-page, search-near, search-near-2, read-id, read-id-2, read-turns, read-range, read-range-2, read-range-3, outline, reread). in_view_ask (`view_ask: {target?, turns, budget_tokens}`, the round in `context.audience_set`, `context.session_id`, `context.turn_id`) and the ledger's answers to its phases (view-rows, view-blocks) -- only reads, at most two rounds. in_seed_ask (the handle `hop.live`/`context.live` of the running session, `hop.renewal_n`, the round in `context.audience_set`) and its phases (seed-rows, seed-blocks); in_part (`{target, source, value, subject?, until?}`, `value` kept unread) and in_seed_line (`{live|session_id, position, order, lasts, text}`), each one `state` write (phase state-write), answered by nothing. in_live_end (#1369: the handle `hop.live`/`context.live`, `hop.session_id`, the round in `context.audience_set`) and its phases (live-facts-rows, live-facts-blocks). in_view_ask with `context.delta` "1" (a partial of a voice turn, under the call's id) reads the round's rows whatever their session, like in_seed_ask, and ages the topic against the opening of the running session (`context.live`).
